topics.title: Artie Johnson and Oprah Winfrey
topics.summary: Boy Gary attempts to contact Artie Johnson, a former "Laugh Fan" comedian associated with Ruth Buzzi, leading into a chaotic discussion about celebrity earnings and personal relationships. The conversation veers wildly from Oprah Winfrey’s $500 million income to Judy Garland's past, Goldie Hawn, Alan Soos, and speculation regarding Artie Johnson’s private life, involving bizarre claims like a ‘size queen.’

topics.title: Alan Seuss, Farts & Broadway Chaos
topics.summary: During a chaotic broadcast segment, callers discuss Alan Seuss’s career transition to theater after performing in Catskills shows, leading into bizarre conversations about comparing saloon and elephant farts before transitioning into discussions of Chevy Chase's aloofness and Robin as an intern. The show devolves with multiple attempts to reach Chevy Cornelius via phone.

topics.title: Chevy Chase Phone Call Chaos
topics.summary: During a radio show segment, hosts engage in a chaotic conversation centered around Chevy Chase and his filming of ‘Fletch 2.’ They discuss rumors about his personal life – including past relationships, job details at the Betty Ford Clinic, bizarre questions regarding his behavior, and Cary Grant’s death. The discussion veers into tangents involving other guests like Richard Belzer and Joe Piscopo.

topics.title: Howard & Hollywood Squares
topics.summary: During a radio broadcast, Howard discusses his marriage to a young Russian doctor (around 13-14 years old), referencing Chevy Chase’s film career and potential roles while expressing frustration with Garrett Morris' talent. He makes an outlandish estimate of his own worth ($25 million) and touches on Tom Cruise and the nature of relationships in Hollywood, culminating in a discussion about Scott McKenzie’s song ‘Cocoa.’

topics.title: Confabulations About Pigs, Suicide, Music, and Magazines
topics.summary: The broadcast features a chaotic conversation revolving around various topics including a spiral staircase, a pig named Jaja, George Sanders’ suicide in Spain, the recording industry, Papa John's musical endeavors, Donovan Leech (son of Brian Jones), Charlie Dick (Patty Cline’s husband) and Geraldo Rivera being featured in Playgirl magazine discussing his past sexual behavior. The hosts engage in tangential discussions about Hollywood Squares, Eddie Murphy’s brother, and a Malibu beach outing with no clear narrative or purpose.

topics.title: Papa John's Explicit Fantasies
topics.summary: During the broadcast, host Papa John engages in an inappropriate and explicit discussion about his sexual desires, detailing fantasies involving numerous women including interns and colleagues. He makes crude remarks and references to sex with a disregard for boundaries or sensitivity, leading to uncomfortable exchanges.
